With the help of GPS, they measured that the latitude of mountain peak M was 36.5°N and the elevation was 598m. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a contour topographic map. Mountain peak M is marked with a triangle in the lower slightly middle position of the figure; point P is marked above and to the right of point M, located on the north side of M. Multiple contour lines and elevation labels such as “200” and “500” can be seen on the map. Points P and Q are respectively located in different positions in the figure, and the stem states that the relative height of points P and Q is only 15 m. Reasoning: On the winter solstice, at noon in the Northern Hemisphere, the sun is located in the south, and the shadow of an object should point north; in the figure, P is on the north side of M, so the direction in which the shadow of the pointed top of the pavilion on peak M moves to point P is consistent. According to the contour labels in the figure and in combination with the relative height of P and Q being only 15 m, it can be judged that the elevation of point P is about 315 m. The elevation of peak M is 598 m, and Guanyun Pavilion is about 5 m high, so the elevation of the pavilion tip is about 598+5=603 m. The vertical height difference from the pavilion tip to the ground at point P is about 603-315=288 m. The latitude of Zaozhuang is 36.5°N, and on the winter solstice the direct solar point is about 23.5°S, so the noon solar altitude angle is 90°-(36.5°+23.5°)=30°. Therefore, the horizontal distance between P and M is about 288/tan30°≈288×1.73≈500 m.

Two groups of students respectively arrived at points P and Q, and measured and calculated that the relative height of the two points was only 15m. ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: The figure is a contour topographic map. Mountain peak M is marked with a triangle in the lower slightly middle position of the figure; point P is marked above and to the right of point M, located on the north side of M. Multiple contour lines and elevation labels such as “200” and “500” can be seen on the map. Points P and Q are respectively located in different positions in the figure, and the stem states that the relative height of points P and Q is only 15 m.

Reasoning: On the winter solstice, at noon in the Northern Hemisphere, the sun is located in the south, and the shadow of an object should point north; in the figure, P is on the north side of M, so the direction in which the shadow of the pointed top of the pavilion on peak M moves to point P is consistent. According to the contour labels in the figure and in combination with the relative height of P and Q being only 15 m, it can be judged that the elevation of point P is about 315 m. The elevation of peak M is 598 m, and Guanyun Pavilion is about 5 m high, so the elevation of the pavilion tip is about 598+5=603 m. The vertical height difference from the pavilion tip to the ground at point P is about 603-315=288 m. The latitude of Zaozhuang is 36.5°N, and on the winter solstice the direct solar point is about 23.5°S, so the noon solar altitude angle is 90°-(36.5°+23.5°)=30°. Therefore, the horizontal distance between P and M is about 288/tan30°≈288×1.73≈500 m.
